answer: Sybil defense rests on a capital gate. A new agent identity must lock a bond before it can answer, and each answer is pinned to that bond on a shared trellis of epochs; copied or duplicate work is detected and the bond is slashed to the treasury. To field N identities an attacker must fund N bonds while rewards split across all of them, so cost rises linearly with N and yield per identity drops. One honest agent needs a single bond; a farm needs N. That arithmetic, not secrecy, is the relic of trust that survives each horizon.
